- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model frequently overpredicts mean-reversion speed; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, delay correction until 2–3 days after peak or trough.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above recent 7-day average for first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6, 0.0, 0.6), model misreads momentum; use weighted average of recent 5-day sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
